heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 handles Polymaker PolyLite PETG straight out of the box with exceptional reliability and layer bonding. With a conservative max volumetric flow rate of 14 mm³/s, the printer reliably achieves safe sustained printing speeds up to 167 mm/s without requiring an enclosure or nozzle upgrade.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or glue stick as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap Maximum Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s under the Filament Settings to avoid under-extrusion at high print speeds.
Enable 'Avoid Crossing Walls' with a Max Detour Length of 0 to minimize stringing and nozzle oozing over exterior perimeters.
Set Pressure Advance to 0.038 (calibrated via OrcaSlicer dynamic flow calibration) to eliminate corner bulging and seam blobbing.
Lower Part Cooling Fan to 20-50% with Fan Speed Threshold layer times at 30s to maximize layer adhesion and mechanical strength.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe fine whisps and stringing across open travels
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG absorbs moisture rapidly, causing steam micro-explosions in the hotend, paired with overly aggressive travel speeds.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool at 65°C for 6-8 hours, increase travel speed to 500 mm/s, and set retraction distance to 0.8 mm at 30 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: First layer tearing PEI coating upon part removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG forms an aggressive chemical bond with PEI surfaces when directly printed without an interface barrier.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a thin layer of PVP glue stick or liquid glue to the Textured PEI Plate to serve as a sacrificial release agent, and allow the bed to cool below 35°C before part removal.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Burnt material blobs and nozzle dragging through previous layers
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG sticks to the stainless steel nozzle tip due to slight over-extrusion or thermal accumulation, burning and dropping onto the print.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Reduce extrusion multiplier / flow ratio to 0.95 in OrcaSlicer, ensure the silicone sock is intact, and enable 0.2 mm Z-hop on retraction.

faq.question: Can I print Polymaker PolyLite PETG on the Bambu Lab A1 without an enclosure?
faq.answer: Yes, PolyLite PETG does not require an enclosure and performs reliably in open-frame printers since it does not suffer from extreme thermal shrinkage like ABS or ASA.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade to a hardened steel nozzle to print PolyLite PETG?
faq.answer: No, standard PolyLite PETG is non-abrasive, so the stock Bambu Lab A1 stainless steel nozzle provides full longevity without premature wear.

faq.question: Why is my maximum printing speed limited to 167 mm/s?
faq.answer: The 167 mm/s limit is calculated from the hotend volumetric melt ceiling of 14 mm³/s at standard 0.2mm layer height and 0.42mm line width to prevent under-extrusion and weak interlayer bonds.

faq.question: Can I use the Bambu Lab AMS Lite directly with this filament?
faq.answer: Yes, Polymaker PolyLite PETG cardboard spools work well with the AMS Lite, though printing an external plastic spool adapter ring is recommended to prevent cardboard rim degradation during rewinding.
